observation: Product-workflow imagery is treated as evidence below the proposition. The mobile capture keeps the message readable while the product view is cropped.
adapt: Show the actual operation or artifact when evaluating a tool.
reject: Copying the dark palette, recognizable UI, partner logos or copy cadence.
limitations: Homepage states only; no signup or application workflow tested. Initial capture was blurred during entrance; a later capture resolved it.

observation: The object and its lighting dominate the scene. Desktop navigation is dense while mobile reduces the chrome.
adapt: Let a strong actual product asset carry identity before adding explanatory ornament.
reject: Copying iconography, language, dramatic shadows or sparse information when another product needs clear specifications.
limitations: No commerce actions or navigation were exercised.

observation: A programme-led scene connects the place to cultural activity. Mobile keeps a booking action near the bottom while the content continues below.
adapt: Connect atmosphere to a concrete activity and next action rather than showing place photography alone.
reject: Automatically adopting a carousel, floating controls, uppercase identity or persistent bar.
limitations: No booking or programme action was tested; no accessibility/performance claim.

observation: Project evidence and a discipline/sector expression lead the visible composition.
adapt: Let actual work and useful taxonomy explain a practice.
reject: Copying its signature layout or assuming all portfolios need the same treatment.
limitations: Consent notice obscures part of the view, especially mobile. No filter or navigation behavior verified.

observation: The visible campaign combines a domestic scene, product-family emphasis and a sofa exploration path.
adapt: Connect objects to context and a real product choice.
reject: Treating its large type, colors or presentation as a furniture template.
limitations: Consent dialog obscures substantial content. The full campaign and interactions were not verified.

observation: The captured first view is a customer/region gate over an interior scene.
adapt: Recognize entry barriers as part of the actual visitor experience.
reject: Claiming the catalogue was visually reviewed from this gate.
limitations: No region selection or catalogue interaction performed; mobile image captured but not used for visual conclusions.

observation: Content extraction exposed product and material taxonomy, but browser access returned HTTP 403 and a security challenge.
adapt: Content taxonomy can be investigated separately from composition.
reject: Claiming knowledge of the current visual arrangement from extracted text.
limitations: Not a usable visual reference in this session.

observation: The captured page shows navigation but the main visual region did not render, including after a longer settling interval.
adapt: A successful HTTP status is not proof of a successfully inspected visual state.
reject: Describing unseen photography or animation from brand reputation.
limitations: Not retained as a full visual reference; content/navigation extraction only.
